leftEvidence.title: Pardon is granted while the unbelieving generation is excluded

points.label: Event action and claim
points.left: The LORD says, “I have pardoned according to your word,” yet declares that those who tested him and did not listen will not see the land.
points.right: God brings Israel from Egypt, gives statutes and Sabbaths, and recalls rebellion in the wilderness.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: Caleb is singled out for another spirit and full following; Israel is told to turn toward the wilderness.
points.right: He says he swore not to bring them into the given land because they rejected his judgments, yet his eye spared them from complete destruction.

payload.posture: Numbers holds pardon beside exclusion; Ezekiel remembers an oath of non-entry beside God sparing the people from complete destruction.

rightEvidence.role: Refusal remembered as unbelief and lost rest
rightEvidence.title: Ezekiel remembers the wilderness oath and divine restraint

payload.tension: Ezekiel summarizes a wider rebellion field and does not isolate the spies’ report as its only referent.
payload.title: Pardon, preservation, and exclusion
